chapter: Kirby again, Garland gigs and later recordings
title: Charlie Ventura's bop band replaced by Kirby in Milwaukee
summary: The Milwaukee club hated Ventura's bebop, which Holmes admired, and hired Kirby's popular-song band to finish the engagement.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: In the meantime, Charlie Ventura's band opened in... I will call this club the Cosmopolitan Club in Milwaukee. That's not the name of it, but that's what I'll call it -- because I don't remember the name of it! Anyway, Charlie Ventura's band followed Kirby's band in there. Well, Kirby had a band that most folks could sing along with. We played popular numbers, numbers that people knew, that they could sing. And then he played his little Society numbers, too. And then would come Swing, the Swing numbers. Well, we
would use a variety. So people liked it very much.

But Charlie Ventura's band, they come in there with strictly Bop, Bebop. And at that time, Bop wasn't too popular -- at that time. And they didn't understand what Charile Ventura was doing. They didn't understand it at all. People didn't like it. The bosses didn't like it. And to me, Charlie Ventura and his group sounded like a million dollars -- to me. And they didn't like it.

So when the boss found out that Kirby's band was laying off in Chicago, the boss come down there and hired Kirby to come up there and fill out this engagement of Charlie Ventura -- because he was going to let him go right away. So we went back there and they let Charlie go, and we finished out his engagement. Because they didn't like him. He was one of the people working there. And we went back, and I think we stayed back there three weeks.
